Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation, attached is a compact proposal that aligns cost and performance for RoadRunner's inference footprint while giving you an option to accelerate savings by prepaying. High-level summary: 

- Term: 2 years (invoiced annually, prepay on each anniversary)
- Year 1 prepaid amount: $1,200,000 (covers committed units at an effective 18% discount vs list)
- Year 2 prepaid amount: $1,000,000 (effective 12% discount vs list)
- Ramp: monthly smoothing schedule across each year; we expect peak utilization in Q4 of each year
- Volume flexibility: allow a one-time down-adjust up to 20% in Year 2 (pro-rata reconciliation at year-end)
- SLA / performance credit: automated credits for latency or availability misses — proposed cap 5% monthly of that month’s invoice; we discussed an elevated credit if latency breaches repeat, to be handled in the SLA exceptions appendix

Attachments: RR_Proposal_2yr_accelprepay_v3.pdf, SLA-Exceptions-Chart.xlsx. I flagged the specific sections on the billing timing and the flexibility bucket your procurement asked about.

Next steps: if this shape looks reasonable I can put the term sheet into DocuSign and kick off procurement-friendly deliverables (PO template, invoice schedule). If you want to tighten the Year 2 flexibility (e.g., reduce to 10%) or request a different credit cap, note it here and I’ll route it for internal approval.

Thanks —
Mina

Mina —

Appreciate the clean summary and the quick turn. A few points we need clarified before I run this to legal/procurement: 

1) Year 2 reduction: we want the ability to reduce committed units by up to 20% but would like an explicit mechanism for applying any unused prepay back as a credit or a refund against Year 2 invoicing.
2) SLA credits: 5% monthly cap is reasonable, but given our scale we’d ask for a 7% credit in the event of two consecutive monthly breaches, with a 2-month cumulative cap per year.
3) Billing timing: can we consider a 60/40 split (60% on day 1 of each year, remainder at month 6) to match our internal cash planning?

If you can confirm the above or propose a compromise I’ll escalate to James and procurement. We’ll also want to see the exact DocuSign envelope before signature.

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the quick feedback and for escalating internally. We ran your requests by finance and sales leadership and here is the agreed shape we can sign to: 

1) Term & money
- 2-year commitment, invoiced annually with prepay at each anniversary.
- Year 1 prepaid amount: $1,200,000 (effective ~18% off list).
- Year 2 prepaid amount: $1,000,000 (effective ~12% off list).
- Year 2 flexibility: one-time down-adjust up to 20% of committed units; any unused prepay will be applied as a credit against Year 2 invoices (preferred) — if RoadRunner prefers a cash refund we can discuss but will require CFO sign-off.

2) Billing cadence
- 50/50 split per year billed on Day 1 and Month 7, net-30 payment terms on each invoice.

3) SLA / performance credits
- Standard automated credits remain; for two consecutive monthly breaches we will apply an elevated monthly credit capped at 6% of the affected month’s invoice. Cumulative cap is 3 months per 12-month period. Customer must provide a brief incident report to qualify for escalated credits.

4) Operational guardrails
- If usage exceeds committed units by more than 25% for two consecutive months, we’ll initiate a usage review and may apply temporary rate adjustments until capacity is confirmed.

5) Next steps
- I have uploaded the final term sheet and DocuSign envelope here: https://docusign.com/Envelope/ABC123.
- Attachments: DocuSign_Prepaid_2yr_RR.pdf, RR_Proposal_2yr_accelprepay_v3.pdf, SLA-Exceptions-Chart.xlsx.
- Please send PO and sign the DocuSign envelope. Once DocuSign is complete I will push the deal into HubSpot (DEAL-78912) and Laura will issue internal approval.

If this looks good I’ll send the DocuSign link directly to James and procurement and loop legal for a quick review. Thanks again — appreciate the partnership.
